newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: AsianBank, PDCP terminate merger plan.
newsitem.headline: AsianBank, PDCP terminate merger plan.

text.p: AsianBank Corp said on Monday it and PDCP Bank were terminating their planned merger.
"The two banks...were unable to reach an agreement on the respective valuations of the two institutions," AsianBank said in a statement.
PDCP, in a separate statement, said the collapse of the negotiations was due to "differences of opinion in approaches to the valuation methods."

The merger plan was announced last November when major shareholders of the two banks -- Metro Pacific Corp for PDCP Bank and A Soriano Corp and Bacnotan Consolidated Industries of the Phinma Group for AsianBank -- agreed to a merger which would have created the 15th largest commercial bank in the country.
The merged bank would have about 6.6 billion pesos in capital and 140 branches.

"We pursued the merger in the belief that the two institutions would benefit from it, but in the end, in spite of all our efforts towards the merger, both of us concluded that our respective postiions could not be reconciled," AsianBank chairman Ramon del Rosario said.

AsianBank, the bigger of the two banks, wanted to use the status of PDCP Bank as a listed company to raise funds through the stock market. A merger would have spared AsianBank from undergoing the cumbersome listing procedure.
Del Rosario said the AsianBank would revert to its strategy of raising capital through an initial public offering and a partnership with foreign or domestic partners.
PDCP said it would restart negotiations with other groups for a possible tie-up.
"PDCP Bank ... will now reinstigate dialogue with a major foreign financial institution which has expressed interest in investing as a strategic partner with PDCP Bank," the PDCP statement said.
